extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a benchmark for systematically evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It covers five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. Data are drawn from large-scale real robotic datasets and in-house collection across diverse embodiments, objects, and scenes.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo; Chun-Kai Fan; Menghang Dong; Jiayu Shi; Mengdi Zhao; Bo-Wen Zhang; Cheng Chi; Jiaming Liu; Gaole Dai; Rongyu Zhang; Ruichuan An; Kun Wu; Zhengping Che; Shaoxuan Xie; Guocai Yao; Zhongxia Zhao; Pengwei Wang; Guang Liu; Zhongyuan Wang; Tiejun Huang; Shanghang Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang. RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv:2510.17801, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Datasets were built from open-source large-scale real robotic datasets and in-house curated collection. Planning data was drawn from high-quality robotic videos across multiple sources. Perception data was constructed using real robot data with type and view metadata, curated static object attributes, GPT-generated functional properties, Gemini-segmented video steps, and manual annotations. Affordance data was sampled from the planning pool and annotated with contact points, motion trajectories, and base positions. Failure analysis data for execution-level errors was collected from RoboMIND and labeled by experts; planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Software Collection; User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Planning-level failure data was noted as unavailable from real-world sources, so those samples were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real robotic datasets including Open X-Embodiment (Collaboration et al., 2023), RH20T (Fang et al., 2023), RoboMIND (Wu et al., 2024), and others (Lin et al., 2024a; Liu et al., 2024b,c; Mu et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2024; Bu et al., 2025); in-house collected robotic videos; curated static object attribute data (Gao et al., 2024); robot type and view metadata from real robot data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 professionally trained annotators conducted comprehensive quality inspections validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. For planning tasks, Gemini generated structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata) which were refined by human annotators. Scene-centric perception data included manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes. Task-centric data used human-labeled bounding boxes. Execution-level failure data was labeled by experts. A majority-vote strategy was applied: items all models solve correctly were removed, and items all models fail were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A majority-vote strategy was used: items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction. Human evaluation of planning was conducted by expert annotators who assigned holistic scores (0–20) referencing ground-truth planning lists and considering skill selection, object identification, and plan executability.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini (for generating structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata; also used for video segmentation for temporal grounding); GPT (for generating functional object properties and distractors for object-centric perception data; for rewriting explicit instructions into implicit forms using LLMs)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data; existing planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left–right arm assignments or positional movements, limiting cross-embodiment evaluation
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation; benchmarking high-level cognition across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis; guiding the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Planning-level failure examples are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data. Implicit instructions are generated by rewriting explicit instructions into demand-based requests using LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A two-stage quality control process is applied: during construction, general filters address image quality and task validity, while sub-benchmark-specific filters exclude inappropriate data (e.g., single-arm data from dual-arm tasks). After construction, 20 professionally trained annotators validate linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is applied: items all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail are manually reviewed and corrected. Robot videos are converted into natural language task descriptions with frame-level step annotations using Gemini, then refined by human annotators. Steps are mapped into predefined function templates and instantiated with object references.
